name: Democratic socialism
summary: Democratic socialism is the family of socialisms that seek social ownership or democratic control of the economy while keeping political democracy, and that reject authoritarian Marxist-Leninist rule and the command economy. Its defining scholarship also stresses equality, social justice and extending democracy into the workplace. The defining sources are thin on the rest of the test.
scope: Family entry answered only from sources defining the family as such: the Stanford Encyclopedia entry on socialism (its democratic-socialist passages and definition of socialism), the Oxford World Encyclopedia entry, and the ECPS glossary (which relays an Oxford Reference definition and Keith Dixon), Newman and Sears. No party programme, member thinker or survey of members is used; social democracy, market socialism, libertarian socialism and Eurocommunism have their own entries. Newman, Socialism: A Very Short Introduction (2005) and Sears, Socialism 101 (2019), supplied by the maintainer. Newman has no democratic socialism section, so only what he says of all socialists is used. Sassoon, March and Harrington were not available; Britannica returned 403.

furtherReading.title: Socialism (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
furtherReading.note: Careful introduction to socialist ideals, critiques of capitalism and institutional designs.

furtherReading.title: Democratic Socialism (ECPS glossary)
furtherReading.note: Short glossary entry on what the label means and how it differs from social democracy.

sources.title: Socialism
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Definition of socialism as social, democratic control of the means of production; democratic socialists extending democracy into the economy; planning and market socialism debates.

sources.title: Democratic socialism (World Encyclopedia, Oxford)
sources.author: Encyclopedia.com / Oxford University Press
sources.usedFor: Principles: equality and social justice, parliamentary government, redistribution through progressive taxation, social protection.

sources.title: Socialism: A Very Short Introduction
sources.author: Michael Newman
sources.usedFor: Oxford University Press, 2005 (the link is the publisher page of the 2nd edition). General definition of socialism (egalitarianism, challenge to capitalist property, solidarity and cooperation); it has no separate democratic socialism section, so only claims it makes of all socialists are used.

sources.title: Socialism 101
sources.author: Kathleen Sears (Adams Media)
sources.usedFor: Adams Media, 2019 (publisher catalog page). Popular introduction: social ownership of socially produced goods; production for public good not private profit; personal belongings stay private. Medium confidence at most.

sources.title: Democratic Socialism (glossary)
sources.author: European Center for Populism Studies
sources.usedFor: Relays an Oxford Reference definition (social ownership plus political democracy, against Soviet models) and Keith Dixon on freedom; medium confidence at most, parts echo encyclopedic summaries.
